stem: Which of the following is an odd number?
hint: An odd number is not divisible by 2.
explanation: 14 ÷ 2 = 7 (even), 22 ÷ 2 = 11 (even), 37 ÷ 2 = 18.5 — not whole, so 37 is odd, 40 ÷ 2 = 20 (even). Answer: 37.
source: ETS Official GRE Guide — Number Properties (even/odd rules, primes, divisibility)

stem: If x is an odd integer and y is an even integer, what is x + y?
hint: Try small examples: 3 + 4.
explanation: Odd + even = odd. 3 + 4 = 7; 11 + 2 = 13. An odd plus an even always gives an odd result.
source: ETS Official GRE Guide — Number Properties (even/odd rules, primes, divisibility)

stem: If a is an even integer and b is an even integer, what is a × b?
hint: Multiply two small evens: 2 × 4.
explanation: Even × even = even. 2 × 4 = 8; 6 × 10 = 60. The product of two even integers is always even.
source: ETS Official GRE Guide — Number Properties (even/odd rules, primes, divisibility)

stem: Which of the following sums is odd?
hint: odd + odd = even; even + odd = odd.
explanation: 8 + 12 = 20 (even), 7 + 9 = 16 (even), 15 + 22 = 37 (odd — even added to odd gives odd), 30 + 44 = 74 (even). Answer: 15 + 22.
source: ETS Official GRE Guide — Number Properties (even/odd rules, primes, divisibility)

stem: If n is an odd integer, which of the following must be even?
hint: Add 1 to an odd number and check parity.
explanation: n = 3: n + 1 = 4 (even), n + 2 = 5 (odd), 2n + 1 = 7 (odd), n = 3 (odd). Only n + 1 is guaranteed even for any odd n.
source: ETS Official GRE Guide — Number Properties (even/odd rules, primes, divisibility)

stem: The product of three odd integers is:
hint: Multiply 3 × 5 × 7.
explanation: Odd × odd = odd, and odd × odd = odd again. 3 × 5 × 7 = 105, odd. Any count of odd factors multiplied together gives an odd product.
source: ETS Official GRE Guide — Number Properties (even/odd rules, primes, divisibility)

stem: Which of the following is a prime number?
hint: A prime has exactly two factors: 1 and itself.
explanation: 9 = 3 × 3, 15 = 3 × 5, 17 has only factors 1 and 17 (prime), 21 = 3 × 7. Answer: 17.
source: ETS Official GRE Guide — Number Properties (even/odd rules, primes, divisibility)

stem: What is the smallest prime number?
hint: Check which has exactly two factors.
explanation: 0 is not prime, 1 has only one factor (not prime), 2 has factors 1 and 2 (prime). 2 is the smallest prime — and the only even prime.
source: ETS Official GRE Guide — Number Properties (even/odd rules, primes, divisibility)

stem: How many prime numbers are there between 10 and 20?
hint: List candidates and test each: 11–19.
source: Manhattan Prep 5 lb. Book of GRE Practice Problems — Number Properties (factors, multiples, remainders)

stem: Which of the following numbers is NOT prime?
hint: Test each for factors besides 1 and itself.
explanation: 2, 13, 29 are prime. 39 = 3 × 13, so 39 is not prime.
source: ETS Official GRE Guide — Number Properties (even/odd rules, primes, divisibility)

stem: Which of the following is the prime factorization of 36?
hint: Break 36 into factors until only primes remain.
explanation: 36 = 6 × 6 = (2 × 3) × (2 × 3) = 2 × 2 × 3 × 3. Only the third choice uses all prime factors.
source: Manhattan Prep 5 lb. Book of GRE Practice Problems — Number Properties (factors, multiples, remainders)

stem: Which of the following numbers has exactly two prime factors (counting repeats)?
hint: Factor each completely and count.
source: ETS Official GRE Guide — Number Properties (even/odd rules, primes, divisibility)

stem: The number 1 is:
hint: A prime needs exactly two distinct factors.
explanation: 1 has only one factor (itself), so it is not prime. It is not composite either. So 1 is neither prime nor composite.
source: ETS Official GRE Guide — Number Properties (even/odd rules, primes, divisibility)

stem: How many positive factors does 12 have?
hint: List every number that divides 12 evenly.
explanation: Factors of 12: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12. That is 6 positive factors.
source: Manhattan Prep 5 lb. Book of GRE Practice Problems — Number Properties (factors, multiples, remainders)

stem: Which of the following is a multiple of 7?
hint: Divide each by 7.
source: Manhattan Prep 5 lb. Book of GRE Practice Problems — Number Properties (factors, multiples, remainders)

stem: What is the greatest common factor (GCF) of 18 and 24?
hint: List each number's factors and pick the largest shared one.
source: Manhattan Prep 5 lb. Book of GRE Practice Problems — Number Properties (factors, multiples, remainders)

stem: What is the least common multiple (LCM) of 4 and 6?
hint: List multiples of each until one matches.
explanation: Multiples of 4: 4, 8, 12, 16… Multiples of 6: 6, 12, 18… The smallest shared multiple is 12.
source: Manhattan Prep 5 lb. Book of GRE Practice Problems — Number Properties (factors, multiples, remainders)

stem: If 5 is a factor of n, which of the following must be a multiple of n?
hint: Every number is a multiple of itself.
explanation: n = 1 × n, so n itself is always a multiple of n. The other choices need not relate to n.
source: Manhattan Prep 5 lb. Book of GRE Practice Problems — Number Properties (factors, multiples, remainders)

stem: How many factors does the prime number 13 have?
hint: Recall the definition of a prime number.
explanation: A prime has exactly two factors: 1 and itself. So 13 has 2 factors.
source: ETS Official GRE Guide — Number Properties (even/odd rules, primes, divisibility)

stem: Which of the following pairs are both multiples of 9?
hint: Check each number by dividing by 9.
explanation: 18 ÷ 9 = 2 ✓ and 27 ÷ 9 = 3 ✓. 19 and 38 are not divisible by 9. Answer: 18 and 27.
source: Manhattan Prep 5 lb. Book of GRE Practice Problems — Number Properties (factors, multiples, remainders)

stem: Which of the following numbers is divisible by 3?
hint: Add the digits — if the sum is divisible by 3, so is the number.
source: ETS Official GRE Guide — Number Properties (even/odd rules, primes, divisibility)

stem: Which of the following numbers is divisible by 5?
hint: A number is divisible by 5 if its last digit is 0 or 5.
explanation: 123 ends in 3, 237 ends in 7, 340 ends in 0 (yes), 412 ends in 2. Answer: 340.
source: ETS Official GRE Guide — Number Properties (even/odd rules, primes, divisibility)

stem: Which of the following numbers is divisible by 4?
hint: A number is divisible by 4 if its last two digits form a multiple of 4.
source: ETS Official GRE Guide — Number Properties (even/odd rules, primes, divisibility)

stem: Which of the following numbers is divisible by 9?
hint: Add the digits — if the sum is a multiple of 9, the number is divisible by 9.
source: ETS Official GRE Guide — Number Properties (even/odd rules, primes, divisibility)

stem: Which of the following numbers is divisible by both 2 and 3?
hint: Divisible by 2 → even; divisible by 3 → digit sum divisible by 3.
source: ETS Official GRE Guide — Number Properties (even/odd rules, primes, divisibility)

stem: Which of the following numbers is divisible by 10?
hint: Divisible by 10 means the last digit is 0.
explanation: Only 2,340 ends in 0.
source: ETS Official GRE Guide — Number Properties (even/odd rules, primes, divisibility)

stem: What is the remainder when 17 is divided by 5?
hint: 5 × 3 = 15; subtract from 17.
explanation: 5 × 3 = 15. 17 − 15 = 2. The remainder is 2.
source: Manhattan Prep 5 lb. Book of GRE Practice Problems — Number Properties (factors, multiples, remainders)

stem: What is the remainder when an even number is divided by 2?
hint: Even numbers are divisible by 2 by definition.
explanation: An even number divided by 2 leaves no remainder: e.g., 14 ÷ 2 = 7 remainder 0.
source: Manhattan Prep 5 lb. Book of GRE Practice Problems — Number Properties (factors, multiples, remainders)

stem: When 43 is divided by 6, the remainder is:
hint: 6 × 7 = 42; subtract from 43.
explanation: 6 × 7 = 42. 43 − 42 = 1. The remainder is 1.
source: Manhattan Prep 5 lb. Book of GRE Practice Problems — Number Properties (factors, multiples, remainders)

stem: If n divided by 4 leaves a remainder of 3, which of the following could be n?
hint: Divide each by 4 and check the remainder.
source: Manhattan Prep 5 lb. Book of GRE Practice Problems — Number Properties (factors, multiples, remainders)
